== Introduction: The Map of Computational Physics ==
In the [[The Principia Machina|Principia Machina]], we test whether physical reality can be derived from single, elegant action principles—such as Hamilton's Principle (<math>\delta S = 0</math>). However, translating mathematical actions into concrete predictions requires different computational weapons depending on the nature of the physical realm.

== The Four Paradigms of Computational Physics ==

=== 1. Symbolic Equation Discovery (The AI Prospectors) ===
* '''Tools:''' [[The Principia Machina/Tools/PySR|PySR]], [[The Principia Machina/Tools/AIFeynman|AI Feynman]]
* '''Plain-Language Metaphor:''' Imagine looking at a table of planetary motion data without knowing Kepler's or Newton's laws. Symbolic regression engines act as automated theoretical physicists. They scan raw data to discover analytical mathematical formulas, testing millions of combinations to find the simplest equation that perfectly explains the observations without overfitting.
* '''Role in SVD:''' Automatically discovering the mathematical form of the Lagrangian scalar <math>\mathcal{L}</math> from simulated vacuum field fluctuations.

=== 2. Neural Action & PDE Solvers (The Variational Approximators) ===
* '''Tools:''' [[The Principia Machina/Tools/DeepXDE|DeepXDE]]
* '''Plain-Language Metaphor:''' Traditional PDE solvers divide space into rigid grid squares. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) treat neural networks as flexible mathematical surfaces. Instead of guessing values at grid points, the neural network adjusts its parameters until the underlying physical laws—or the principle of least action—are satisfied everywhere simultaneously.
* '''Role in SVD:''' Mesh-free solving of non-linear field equations across intricate boundary conditions by directly minimizing the Action Integral.

=== 3. High-Performance Field Compilers (The Wave Engines) ===
* '''Tools:''' [[The Principia Machina/Tools/Devito|Devito]], [[The Principia Machina/Tools/FiPy|FiPy]], [[The Principia Machina/Tools/Clawpack|Clawpack]]
* '''Plain-Language Metaphor:''' Simulating continuous wave dynamics—such as light waves, acoustic ripples, or fluid shocks—requires massive computational power. Tools like Devito take high-level symbolic field equations (e.g., Maxwell's vector equations) and automatically generate hyper-optimized C code for parallel supercomputers.
* '''Role in SVD:''' High-speed numerical testing of wave propagation, Maxwellian displacement currents, and vacuum field disturbances.

=== 4. Tensor & Variational Algebras (The Symbolic Architects) ===
* '''Tools:''' [[The Principia Machina/Tools/Cadabra2|Cadabra2]], [[The Principia Machina/Tools/FEniCS|FEniCS]], [[The Principia Machina/Tools/ModelingToolkit|ModelingToolkit.jl]]
* '''Plain-Language Metaphor:''' These tools carry out the exact mathematical steps a theoretical physicist performs on paper—taking action variations, contracting tensor indices in general relativity, or converting field equations into solvable matrix operations.
* '''Role in SVD:''' Deriving Euler-Lagrange field equations directly from action candidate postulates.
